key_concepts: An ecosystem consists of interacting biotic and abiotic factors in a geographic area
Rainforests have the highest biodiversity and form stable ecosystems
Human activities can have both positive and negative effects on ecosystems
Monoculture increases crop yields but can deprive animals of food and habitat
Pesticides and herbicides control pests and weeds but can pollute air, water, and soil
Deforestation can support modernization but causes habitat loss, erosion, flooding, and cl
Overhunting reduces species populations and can lead to extinction
Pollution from improper waste disposal harms living organisms and ecosystems
Land conversion supports socioeconomic growth but causes habitat destruction and land degr
Recycling, reforestation, tree planting, and waste segregation help restore ecosystems
Digging planting holes properly involves marking, loosening soil, removing rocks and roots
